data.problem: Bad Request (400) responses for claude-opus-4-5 via opencode provider; need to identify failing parameter and align thinking/effort mapping while preserving variant behavior.
constraints: Avoid logging secrets; sanitize headers and message content.
Keep upstream variant behavior intact while mapping agent.thinking.

options.name: Instrument request + error logging for Anthropic/opencode
options.approach: Add safe logs in LLM.stream after params/options are built (capture modelID, providerID, variant, thinking/effort fields, maxOutputTokens) and extend onError to capture provider error payload/status (redacting headers and message content). Run a failing request to capture exact payload.
options.what_we_learn: Exact outgoing params and error body, confirming which field triggers 400.
options.risk_if_wrong: Low; adds temporary logging but does not change behavior.

options.name: Config-only isolation run
options.approach: Run local requests with agent.thinking disabled and with/without --variant to see if 400 persists; then test thinking only vs variant only. Capture error text from session.error events.
options.what_we_learn: Whether thinking budgets or effort mapping are the trigger without code changes.
options.risk_if_wrong: Low; relies on local config toggles.

options.name: Spec alignment audit against Vercel AI SDK
options.approach: Compare current Anthropic effort/thinking shapes to Vercel AI Gateway docs (effort in providerOptions, thinking in thinking {type, budget_tokens}); verify if Opus 4.5 expects output_config or effort-only beta header, and cross-check AI SDK issues on thinking/tool_choice restrictions.
options.what_we_learn: Whether the request shape mismatches upstream expectations and which parameter is out of spec.
options.risk_if_wrong: Medium; could still require empirical logs to confirm.

data.recommendation: Option 1 because it yields the fastest concrete evidence about the exact failing parameter with minimal risk.
